camtrapReport

From camera-trap data to reproducible ecological reports.

camtrapReport turns Camtrap DP datasets into two complementary outputs:

  • Data Status Check: inspect completeness, consistency, annotation, and spatial and temporal coverage before interpreting your data.
  • Ecological Report: combine selected analyses, maps, figures, tables, and explanatory text in a reproducible document.

Work in R or through the optional graphical interface. HTML is the default; static PDF output is also available with compatible modules, the optional pagedown package, and Chrome or Edge.

Available analyses

Choose analyses to match your monitoring question and available measurements.

Area Included analyses
Sampling Study area, camera locations, sampling effort, image and data processing
Species records Captures, capture-based trends, richness, species accumulation
Community and behaviour Co-occurrence and activity patterns
Space and habitat Spatial point-pattern density and habitat preferences
Population density Random Encounter Model (REM) parameters and estimates

Capture rates and spatial point-pattern density are not population-density estimates. REM requires detection, movement, activity, effort, and count data, as well as an appropriate survey design. A module’s availability does not establish its suitability for your dataset. The Ecological Report guide explains the workflow and method-specific requirements.

Install and create your first report

Requires R 4.1.0 or later. Install from GitHub using pak:

if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("spatialecology/camtrapReport")

Some analytical modules require optional packages. Review their #| packages: declarations before installation; explicitly calling camtrapReport::install_all() discovers and installs missing module dependencies, which may be numerous. It is not needed for the small example below. See dependency inspection without installation.

Prepare the input

Use a Camtrap DP directory or ZIP containing datapackage.json, deployments.csv, media.csv, and observations.csv. Keep the tables’ linked identifiers intact. The primary input is a path, not an in-memory list of tables. Use your platform’s Camtrap DP export or upstream Camtrap DP preparation and validation guidance; camtrapReport is not a general arbitrary-table converter or complete schema validator. The package overview explains table relationships, derived sequences, and optional study areas.

The example copies bundled data to a temporary directory because camData() can save a processed-object cache alongside its inputs.

library(camtrapReport)

example_root <- tempfile("camtrapReport-example-")
dir.create(example_root)
stopifnot(file.copy(
  system.file("external", "dataset", package = "camtrapReport"),
  example_root, recursive = TRUE
))
cm <- camData(file.path(example_root, "dataset"), update = TRUE)
#> Warning in cm$setup(): The "suncalc" package is not installed; it is required
#> for the analysis of activity patterns...

Check data, then generate a small report

This deliberately small profile needs no additional analytical packages: three status sections and an introduction-only ecological report.

first_report <- reportProfile(
  name = "first-report",
  report = "introduction",
  status = c("spatial", "temporal", "availability")
)

status_file <- status(
  cm, profile = first_report,
  filename = file.path(example_root, "first-status.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
report_file <- report(
  cm, profile = first_report,
  filename = file.path(example_root, "first-report.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
stopifnot(file.exists(status_file), file.exists(report_file))

Open the returned files, or use view = TRUE when generating them. For fuller illustrations, view the Data Status Check and Ecological Report. Those separate reports may use different data, inputs, profiles, and optional packages; they are not the expected output of this minimal example.

Correct source records when needed, rebuild with cm <- camData(data_path, update = TRUE), then run status() again. Rerunning a report on the existing object does not reread edited CSV/JSON files. Checks identify possible problems; they do not repair records, assign an overall quality grade, or guarantee analytical suitability.

GUI and customisation

Inspect modules, select sections, and update narrative or metadata:

section_names(object = cm, profile = "default")
sections(cm, "introduction")
info(cm, name = c("title", "authors"))

report(cm, filename = file.path(tempdir(), "custom-report.html"))
gui(cm)

Shiny supports gui(); the code workflow does not start an application. Report narrative comes from YAML modules’ text and R code, together with object metadata. Use updateReportSection() or info() for object-level edits, or copy the registry into a writable project folder for reusable module changes. Only load trusted modules: their R code and embedded expressions execute with your session’s permissions. The module guide explains copying, editing, reloading, testing, and sharing modules.

Reusable analytical profiles

Profiles are context-specific, reusable selections of modules and their organisation. They let a project or monitoring network agree on a reporting workflow without imposing one universal analysis on every survey.

  • Default: the standard ecological selection; REM parameters are pooled across years within species, while trap rate remains year-specific.
  • EOW: customised sections for the European Observatory of Wildlife workflow, annual species-by-year REM parameters, and selected status checks in the ecological appendix. Inclusion is not a claim of formal network endorsement.

A profile stores module references and optional parent overrides, not data, fitted models, package versions, or independent parameter settings. Analytical choices live in the referenced modules and object settings; retain those alongside the profile when sharing a reproducible workflow. Pooled and annual REM answer different parameter-sharing questions and can give different estimates. Choose and document the approach; neither is automatically correct for every dataset.

profile_names(cm)
section_names(object = cm, profile = "EOW")
report(
  cm, profile = "EOW",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "EOW-report.html")
)

write_profile("EOW", file.path(tempdir(), "EOW-profile.yml"), object = cm)

For a static PDF, use a .pdf filename or format = "pdf". PDF output has no table of contents; printable tab panels are expanded. The registry’s formats column controls module compatibility. See the Profiles guide for creating, editing, importing, and exporting profiles.

A community knowledge hub of reviewed analytical workflows is a future direction, not a currently implemented service. Projects can already share profiles with their required module files and documented settings through normal version-controlled collaboration.

Technical guidance and interpretation

Continue with the guide that matches your next task:

  • Package overview: input relationships, cache files, object structure, scope, and reproducibility.
  • Data Status Check: review checks and repeat them after corrections.
  • Ecological Report: filters, years, methods, report timing, PDF output, and map backgrounds.
  • Profiles and module management: reuse workflows or develop trusted extensions.
  • Function reference: exact arguments and return values.

Retain input data, optional inputs, analytical settings, module/profile versions, and software versions. Interpret results in light of sampling effort, detectability, season, habitat, and method-specific assumptions. Diagnostic test = TRUE can omit failed sections; it is not a substitute for successful full analyses. The default offline map background needs no tile service; online backgrounds depend on provider permissions and availability.

When taxize is installed, import may query GBIF automatically; the current API has no per-call opt-out. This can affect privacy, offline use, and reproducibility. Reports can reveal sensitive species locations; review them before sharing. See the overview for details on these limits and caches.

The bundled example is a relationship-preserving subset of GMU8_LEUVEN, intended for software demonstration and testing, not ecological inference (provenance and preparation).

Citation, development, and support

Developed and maintained by Elham Ebrahimi. Use citation("camtrapReport") for the software and associated paper entries.

Development has drawn on real monitoring datasets and independent user feedback across regions, including European monitoring networks; see publications and training resources. The package complements data-management and analysis tools such as camtrapdp, camtraptor, camtrapR, and ct.

Report an issue or read the contributing guide and code of conduct before contributing a module, profile, documentation improvement, or fix.
